I enjoy the meta of bloggers writing about their blogging setup. So here's mine.

![](image.jpg)

### Why Quarto

Quarto is a publishing system built on top of Pandoc. It renders Markdown, R Markdown, and Jupyter notebooks into websites, PDFs, or slide decks. For a data scientist, that means you can write a post that includes real code, real output, and real figures — all in one document, with no copy-pasting.

The previous generation of this was R Markdown, which worked well but was R-only. Quarto is language-agnostic: Python, R, Julia, and Observable all work.

### Jupyter notebooks as posts

One thing I particularly like: you can use `.ipynb` files directly as posts. Write your analysis in a notebook, add a YAML header, and Quarto publishes it. No conversion step, no reformatting.

This matters because it keeps the source of truth in one place. The notebook is the post.

### The setup

This site is built with:

- **Quarto** for rendering
- **GitHub Actions** for automated deployment on every push
- **GitHub Pages** for hosting

The workflow is simple: write a post, push to `main`, and it goes live. The whole pipeline is [visible in the repo](https://github.com/SebasEliens/dase).

### What I'd change

The main friction so far is freezing: Quarto caches executed outputs so you don't re-run expensive code on every build. That's good in principle but occasionally produces stale outputs if you're not careful. Something to watch.
